1.content:
# Camunda 8.7 — Zeebe Resources & Integrations

Ported from the Camunda Grafana dashboard `8.7.35-zeebe.json`. Metrics are expected in Grail as **Micrometer meter names** (`zeebe.stream.processor.records.total`), pushed straight from Camunda over OTLP with `delta` temporality — see `runbook-dynatrace.md`.

**Companion dashboards:** `8.7-zeebe-01-overview.json` · `8.7-zeebe-02-processing.json` · `8.7-zeebe-03-storage.json` · `8.7-zeebe-04-cluster.json`

2.content:
## Memory
JVM heap/non-heap, buffer pools, Netty and GC.

3.title: Process memory usage
3.query:
timeseries {
    rss = avg(dt.kubernetes.container.memory_working_set, filter:{matchesValue(k8s.pod.name, "*zeebe*") and matchesValue(k8s.container.name, "zeebe*")}),
    limit_v = max(dt.kubernetes.container.limits_memory, filter:{matchesValue(k8s.pod.name, "*zeebe*") and matchesValue(k8s.container.name, "zeebe*")}),
    request = min(dt.kubernetes.container.requests_memory, filter:{matchesValue(k8s.pod.name, "*zeebe*") and matchesValue(k8s.container.name, "zeebe*")})
  },
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace))},
  union: true
3.description: Memory limits and requests are taken from the k8 pod metrics.

4.title: JVM Memory usage
4.query:
timeseries {
    used = sum(jvm.memory.used, filter:{area == "heap"}),
    committed = sum(jvm.memory.committed, filter:{area == "heap"}),
    max_v = sum(jvm.memory.max, filter:{area == "heap"})
  },
  by: {k8s.pod.name},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true
4.description:
Total amount of memory reserved for the JVM, where:

- Used means currently in use by live objects
- Committed means allocated to the JVM by the OS, and guaranteed to be available for usage
- Max means maximum possible committed memory, but not guaranteed

Dropped query: pre-Micrometer name, dead in 8.7: jvm_memory_bytes_used

5.title: Buffer Pool Memory Usage
5.description: Dropped query: pre-Micrometer name, dead in 8.7: jvm_buffer_pool_used_bytes

6.title: Netty pooled allocated bytes
6.description: The amount of memory allocated by Netty's pooled allocator

7.title: Netty unpooled allocated bytes
7.description: The amount of memory allocated by Netty's unpooled allocator

8.title: GC Count per second
8.query:
timeseries {
    p50 = percentile(jvm.gc.pause, 50),
    p90 = percentile(jvm.gc.pause, 90),
    p99 = percentile(jvm.gc.pause, 99)
  },
  by: {k8s.pod.name},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true
8.description:
Shows the number of garbage collections (GC) per second, aggregated per pod and GC type.

Ported from Grafana: Grafana rated the GC histogram's observation count (`jvm_gc_pause_seconds_count`). Grail cannot query a histogram's observation count, so this charts GC pause duration percentiles instead.

9.title: GC proportion per second
9.description:
Shows the garbage collection (GC) time proportion per second. Means shows the rate which is spent in GC in a second.

Ported from Grafana: Time spent in GC per second, from the sum of the GC pause histogram. Verify in your tenant that `sum()` over a histogram returns the sum of observations; if it does not, use `percentile(jvm.gc.pause, 99)` as a proxy.

10.content:
## CPU
Container CPU usage, throttling and JVM threads.

11.title: CPU Throttling (AVG)
11.description:
The average percentage of CPU periods where the container ran but was throttled (stopped from running the whole CPU period).


container_cpu_cfs_periods_total -
Number of elapsed enforcement period intervals
container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total -
Number of throttled period intervals	

https://github.com/google/cadvisor/blob/master/docs/storage/prometheus.md
https://stackoverflow.com/a/67316429/2165134
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UE7QX98-kO0

Ported from Grafana: Grafana computed throttled_periods / periods from cAdvisor. `dt.kubernetes.container.cpu_throttled` is already the throttling ratio (requires Dynatrace Kubernetes monitoring).

12.title: CPU usage

13.title: JVM Thread count
13.query:
timeseries {
    live = sum(jvm.threads.live),
    daemon = sum(jvm.threads.daemon)
  },
  by: {k8s.pod.name},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true
| fieldsAdd non_daemon = live[] - daemon[]
13.description:
Current thread count of a JVM, aggregated by namespace and pod

Ported from Grafana: Grafana used four targets, two of them pre-Micrometer names that are dead in 8.7. This charts live and daemon threads plus their difference in one tile.

15.title: PVC Disk Usage
15.query:
timeseries {
    persistentvolumeclaim_used_a = avg(dt.kubernetes.persistentvolumeclaim.used, default:0, filter:{matchesValue(k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name, "*zeebe*")}),
    persistentvolumeclaim_capacity_b = avg(dt.kubernetes.persistentvolumeclaim.capacity, filter:{matchesValue(k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name, "*zeebe*")})
  },
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace))},
  union: true,
  nonempty: true
| fieldsAdd ratio = persistentvolumeclaim_used_a[] / persistentvolumeclaim_capacity_b[]
| fieldsRemove persistentvolumeclaim_used_a, persistentvolumeclaim_capacity_b

16.title: File descriptors
16.query:
timeseries {
    use_fds = avg(process.files.open),
    limit_v = avg(process.files.max)
  },
  by: {k8s.pod.name},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true

17.title: PVC Disk Available

18.content:
### Container disk & network I/O — not available on this ingest path
The baseline's **Read IOPS**, **Write IOPS**, **Read bytes/s**, **Written bytes/s**, **Network bytes/s transmitted** and **Network bytes/s received** panels read cAdvisor `container_fs_*` / `container_network_*` counters. Camunda's OTLP export does not emit them and Dynatrace has no container-level equivalent.

Use the **Kubernetes** app (workload → containers) for container I/O, or host-level `dt.host.disk.*` / `dt.host.net.*` metrics if OneAgent runs on the nodes.

19.content:
## Elasticsearch Exporter
Elasticsearch exporter flushes and bulk sizes.

20.title: Elasticsearch Exporter (Flush Duration)
20.query:
timeseries {
    p50 = percentile(zeebe.elasticsearch.exporter.flush.duration.seconds, 50),
    p90 = percentile(zeebe.elasticsearch.exporter.flush.duration.seconds, 90),
    p99 = percentile(zeebe.elasticsearch.exporter.flush.duration.seconds, 99)
  },
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(partition, array($Partition))},
  union: true
20.description: Grafana rendered this as a histogram heatmap; Dynatrace charts the p50/p90/p99 percentiles of the same histogram instead.

21.title: Elasticsearch Exporter (Flush Failure Rate)
21.query:
timeseries failed_flush_per_sec = sum(zeebe.elasticsearch.exporter.failed.flush,
    rate:1s),
  by: {k8s.pod.name, partition},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod)) and in(partition, array($Partition))}
21.description:
The rate of failure of flush operations, averaged over 15s intervals

Ported from Grafana: Grafana divided failed flushes by the flush histogram's observation count. Grail cannot query a histogram's observation count, so this shows failed flushes per second rather than a failure ratio.

22.title: Elasticsearch Exporter (Bulk Size)
22.query:
timeseries {
    p50 = percentile(zeebe.elasticsearch.exporter.bulk.size, 50),
    p90 = percentile(zeebe.elasticsearch.exporter.bulk.size, 90),
    p99 = percentile(zeebe.elasticsearch.exporter.bulk.size, 99)
  },
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(partition, array($Partition))},
  union: true
22.description: Grafana rendered this as a histogram heatmap; Dynatrace charts the p50/p90/p99 percentiles of the same histogram instead.

23.title: Elasticsearch Exporter (Bulk Memory Size)

24.title: Elasticsearch disk usage
24.query:
timeseries {
    persistentvolumeclaim_used_a = avg(dt.kubernetes.persistentvolumeclaim.used, default:0, filter:{matchesValue(k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name, "*elastic*")}),
    persistentvolumeclaim_capacity_b = avg(dt.kubernetes.persistentvolumeclaim.capacity, filter:{matchesValue(k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.name, "*elastic*")})
  },
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace))},
  union: true,
  nonempty: true
| fieldsAdd ratio = persistentvolumeclaim_used_a[] / persistentvolumeclaim_capacity_b[]
| fieldsRemove persistentvolumeclaim_used_a, persistentvolumeclaim_capacity_b

26.title: Actor Task Execution Latency
26.query:
timeseries {
    p50 = percentile(zeebe.actor.task.execution.latency, 50),
    p90 = percentile(zeebe.actor.task.execution.latency, 90),
    p99 = percentile(zeebe.actor.task.execution.latency, 99)
  },
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(partition, array($Partition)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true
26.description:
Execution time of a certain actor task.

Grafana rendered this as a histogram heatmap; Dynatrace charts the p50/p90/p99 percentiles of the same histogram instead.

27.title: Actor Job Scheduling Latency
27.query:
timeseries {
    p50 = percentile(zeebe.actor.job.scheduling.latency, 50),
    p90 = percentile(zeebe.actor.job.scheduling.latency, 90),
    p99 = percentile(zeebe.actor.job.scheduling.latency, 99)
  },
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(partition, array($Partition)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true
27.description:
The time between scheduling and executing a job.

Grafana rendered this as a histogram heatmap; Dynatrace charts the p50/p90/p99 percentiles of the same histogram instead.

28.title: Actor Task Execution Latency
28.query:
timeseries {
    p50 = percentile(zeebe.actor.task.execution.latency, 50),
    p99 = percentile(zeebe.actor.task.execution.latency, 99)
  },
  by: {actorName},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod)) and in(partition, array($Partition))},
  union: true
28.description: Execution time of a certain actor task instance and completing it.

29.title: Actor Job Scheduling Latency
29.query:
timeseries {
    p50 = percentile(zeebe.actor.job.scheduling.latency, 50),
    p99 = percentile(zeebe.actor.job.scheduling.latency, 99)
  },
  by: {subscriptionType},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod)) and in(partition, array($Partition))},
  union: true
29.description: The time between scheduling and executing a job.

30.title: Actor Task Execution Count
30.description: Number of times a certain actor task was executed successfully.

31.title: Actor Task Queue Length
31.description: The length of the job queue for an actor task.

32.content:
## Worker Jobs
Java-client job worker activity (requires the worker app to export OTLP).

33.title: Rate of Jobs Activated
33.description: Rate of jobs of jobs activated by the client.

34.title: Rate of Jobs Handled
34.description: Rate of jobs of jobs handled by the worker.

35.title: Number Jobs in "Buffer"
35.query:
timeseries {
    activated = sum(zeebe.client.worker.job.activated, default:0),
    handled = sum(zeebe.client.worker.job.handled, default:0)
  },
  by: {k8s.namespace.name, workerName, jobType},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace))},
  union: true
| fieldsAdd activated_total = arrayCumulativeSum(activated),
            handled_total = arrayCumulativeSum(handled)
| fieldsAdd buffered = activated_total[] - handled_total[]
| fieldsRemove activated, handled, activated_total, handled_total
35.description:
The difference between jobs created and jobs handled.

Ported from Grafana: Both counters arrive as OTLP delta values, so each is cumulated over the timeframe before subtracting -- subtracting the raw deltas would show backlog *growth*, not backlog size. Requires the job worker application to export OTLP as well; the brokers do not emit `zeebe.client.*`.

36.content:
## Job push
Job push from brokers to gateways.

37.title: Broker jobs pushed
37.query:
timeseries {
    pushed_count = sum(zeebe.broker.jobs.pushed.count, rate:1s),
    fail_count = sum(zeebe.broker.jobs.push.fail.count, rate:1s)
  },
  by: {k8s.namespace.name, k8s.pod.name},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true
37.description: The rate of jobs pushed from a broker to a gateway per second, where ✅ are successful pushes, and ❌ are failures

38.title: Gateway jobs pushed rate
38.query:
timeseries {
    push = sum(zeebe.gateway.job.stream.push, rate:1s, filter:{status == "success"}),
    push_2 = sum(zeebe.gateway.job.stream.push, rate:1s, filter:{status == "failure"})
  },
  by: {k8s.namespace.name, k8s.pod.name},
  filter: {in(k8s.namespace.name, array($Namespace)) and in(k8s.pod.name, array($Pod))},
  union: true
38.description: The amount of jobs pushed from the gateway to clients, per second, where ✅ are successful pushes, and ❌ are failures

39.title: Broker job push failed attempt
39.description: The rate of failed job push attempts, grouped by code. Each attempt represents a direct attempt to push the job to a single client, and thus may be higher than the actual number of jobs pushed.

40.title: Gateway job push failed attempt
40.description: The rate of failed job push attempts, grouped by code. Each attempt represents a direct attempt to push the job to a single client, and thus may be higher than the actual number of jobs pushed.

41.title: Jobs pushed by engine
41.description: The rate of jobs activated and pushed by the engine per second

42.content:
## Job stream
Job stream registration between gateways and brokers.

43.title: Gateway client count
43.description: The number of open job stream client calls on the gateway. This should be one per open StreamActivatedJobRequest calls.

44.title: Gateway aggregated stream count
44.description: The number of aggregated streams per gateway. Client streams are logically aggregated as one in a gateway if they would activate the same job with the exact same parameters.

45.title: Broker job stream count
45.description: The count of job streams registered on the broker. This should be the sum of all gateway aggregated streams.

46.title: Gateway registered broker count
46.description: The amount of known brokers (or stream servers) per gateway.
